introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

questions.enonce_markdown: 6. (a) Locate the main relief regions and drainage features of Cameroon from the Adamawa to the Chad Basin. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Relief regions from the Adamawa northwards.**
1. *The Adamawa Plateau* (about 6 to 8 degrees N, about 1,000 m or more): a broad, undulating, granitic plateau across the middle of the country. It is the water divide of Cameroon: the rivers on its southern side drain towards the Atlantic (the Sanaga) and those on its northern side drain towards the Benue (the Niger) and towards Lake Chad.
2. *The Benue basin and the plains and plateaus to its north* (about 8 to 10 degrees N): a lower area of about 200 to 500 m, the valley of the Benue River, with the Lagdo dam and reservoir near Garoua.
3. *The Mandara Mountains* (roughly 10 to 11 degrees N, on the Nigerian border): a mountain chain of volcanic remnants and granite, with rock towers and dense population.
4. *The Diamare plain and the Logone-Chari lowlands (the Chad Basin)* in the far north: a vast, flat, low-lying plain of about 300 m or less, with seasonally flooded areas (the Yaere).

**Drainage features.**
- The *Benue River* rises on the Adamawa Plateau, flows north then west past Garoua and leaves Cameroon for Nigeria, joining the Niger; its tributaries include the Faro, the Mayo Rey and the Kebi.
- The *Logone and Chari rivers* flow northwards along the eastern edge of the far north and join at N'Djamena (Chad), opposite Kousseri, and flow into *Lake Chad*, the inland drainage of the Chad Basin.
- The *mayos* (seasonal rivers) of the north flow in the rainy season and dry up in the dry season.
- *Lake Chad* in the extreme north-east is a shallow lake whose size varies with the rainfall.

*Outline map of Cameroon provided in the paper: the candidate marks and names these features on it.*

**Marking guide.** 1 mark for each relief region or drainage feature correctly located (up to 6).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Briefly describe and explain two physical factors responsible for the uneven distribution of population in Cameroon. *(12 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Distribution (description).** The population is very unevenly distributed: dense in the Western Highlands (West and North West regions), on the slopes of Mount Cameroon, around Douala and Yaounde, and in parts of the Mandara Mountains and the Diamare plain in the Far North; sparse in the forests of the East and South and on the Adamawa Plateau.

**Factor 1 - Relief and altitude (6 marks).**
- High population densities are found in the Western Highlands, where the altitude gives a cool, healthy climate with few malaria mosquitoes and no tsetse fly, and ample rainfall.
- The Mandara Mountains were refuge sites for the people in the past, where terraced slopes support very dense rural populations.
- Steep, rugged or marshy areas (lowland swamps, the steep escarpments) discourage settlement and farming, which leaves them thinly populated.

**Factor 2 - Soils, together with climate (6 marks).**
- *Volcanic soils* of the Western Highlands, of Mount Cameroon and the Moungo area are fertile and support intensive farming (coffee, cocoa, bananas, food crops) and so a dense population.
- By contrast the old, leached, poor soils of the Adamawa and the East and the heavy rainforest give a low density because of poor farm yields and the difficulty of clearing.
- In the far north the low and unreliable rainfall (Sahel) limits density, except around permanent water, as along the Logone.

**Other acceptable factors:** climate and rainfall, vegetation (dense forest), drainage and water supply, disease (tsetse fly and onchocerciasis). Human factors (history, towns, roads, economic activities) support but do not replace the physical factors.

**Marking guide.** For each factor: description of the distribution 2, explanation with reasons 3, example or place 1.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Explain any two social problems faced by Cameroonian towns today. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two problems, each explained and illustrated (2 to 3 marks each):
1. *Housing shortage and slums (unplanned settlement):* rapid rural-urban migration and natural increase have caused a shortage of decent housing, so many people live in overcrowded, spontaneous neighbourhoods on flood-prone or steep land without roads, water, drains or title deeds, as in parts of Douala and Yaounde. Rents are high.
2. *Unemployment and underemployment:* the number of jobs in industry and the formal sector is smaller than the number of job seekers, so many young people work in the informal sector (street trading, motorcycle taxis) with low incomes, which feeds poverty and insecurity.
3. *Inadequate services:* shortage of drinking water, electricity, drainage and waste collection, which leads to flooding, cholera and other diseases, and overcrowded schools and hospitals.
4. *Traffic congestion and insecurity:* too many vehicles on poor roads, pollution and rising crime.

**Marking guide.** Two problems, each explained and illustrated with an example (for instance Douala, Yaounde) for 2 to 3 marks.
